title: Split augmented coherent simplicial diagrams are absolute colimits
statement:
Use the quasicategories, nerves, coherent diagrams, mapping spaces and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in universes large enough for the categories below. Write $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ for $n\geq0$ and $[-1]=\varnothing$. Let $\Delta$ be the ordinary category of the nonempty $[n]$ and monotone maps, and let $\Delta_+$ also include $[-1]$. Let $\Delta_{-\infty}$ have objects $[n]$ for $n\geq-1$ and morphisms the monotone maps $\{-\infty\}\cup[m]\to\{-\infty\}\cup[n]$ fixing the new least element $-\infty$. Embed $\Delta_+$ into this category by extending a monotone map to fix $-\infty$, so that no ordinary element maps to $-\infty$. An augmented coherent simplicial diagram $X:N(\Delta_+)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E$ is called split if it extends to $N(\Delta_{-\infty})^{\mathrm{op}}$. Every such split diagram is a colimit diagram with vertex $X_{-1}$. Explicitly, for every $e\in\mathcal E$, the augmentation induces a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(X_{-1},e)\simeq\lim_{[n]\in\Delta}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(X_n,e).$$
For every coherent functor $Q:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, the augmented diagram $QX$ is also a colimit diagram. No existence of other colimits in either category is assumed.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Notation 4.7.2.1, Definition 4.7.2.2, Remarks 4.7.2.3-4, printed pp. 677-678; the colimit theorem is HTT Lemma 6.1.3.16 as explicitly stated there. Online source read; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Choose a splitting extension $\widetilde X:N(D)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E$, where $D=\Delta_{-\infty}$. Write $j:\Delta\to D$ for adjoining the distinguished least element, and $r:D\to\Delta$ for forgetting which least element is distinguished, while retaining that element in the underlying ordered set. Thus $r([m])=[m+1]$, including $r([-1])=[0]$. A map $j([n])\to[m]$ in $D$ is uniquely determined by its restriction $[n]\to\{-\infty\}\cup[m]=r([m])$; conversely every such monotone restriction extends uniquely by sending the adjoined least element to $-\infty$. This gives bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_D(j([n]),[m])=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([n],r([m]))$. Precomposition and postcomposition are restriction and composition of these same set maps, so the bijections are natural. Hence $j\dashv r$ and $r^{\mathrm{op}}\dashv j^{\mathrm{op}}$. In particular the functor along which we will restrict is the right adjoint $j^{\mathrm{op}}:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$, not $r^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: Notation 4.7.2.1 and Definition 4.7.2.2; agent expansion by the adjoining/forgetting least-element adjunction.

proof.text: Put $J=N(D^{\mathrm{op}})$ and $t=[-1]$. Nerves are identified with the opposite nerves in the statement by reversing strings. The nerve of any ordinary category has inner-horn fillers: consecutive arrows specify a string, its omitted composite is fixed by composition, and associativity makes its other faces agree. The right-pinched mapping space in an ordinary nerve is the discrete simplicial set of arrows, since all arrows in the initial constant face are identities. There is exactly one arrow $[m]\to t$ in $D^{\mathrm{op}}$: oppositely it is the unique pointed monotone map from $\{-\infty\}$ to $\{-\infty\}\cup[m]$. Thus each $\operatorname{Map}_J([m],t)$ is a point, and $t$ is final. The unique arrows define a natural transformation $\mathrm{id}_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}\to\mathrm{const}_t$, since both composites in each naturality square are the unique arrow to $t$. Its nerve, followed by $\widetilde X$, is a coherent cocone $a:\widetilde X\to\Delta_J X_{-1}$ with $a_t=1_{X_{-1}}$.

source.place: Notation 4.7.2.1; explicit ordinary-nerve and terminal-vertex calculation from the definitions.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit], $\widetilde X$ has a colimiting cocone $b$ with vertex $X_{-1}$ and $b_t=1$. We must check the particular cocone $a$, rather than merely the existence of some colimit. For $e\in\mathcal E$ put $H(e)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(\widetilde X,\Delta_J e)$. The dual cocone criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that composition with $b$ gives an equivalence $c_b:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(X_{-1},e)\to H(e)$. Evaluation $v:H(e)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(X_{-1},e)$ at $t$ satisfies $v c_b\simeq1$ because $b_t=1$, so $v$ is an equivalence. Composition with $a$ defines $c_a:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(X_{-1},e)\to H(e)$, and evaluation gives $v c_a\simeq1$ because $a_t=1$. Two-out-of-three now makes $c_a$ an equivalence for every $e$; the same cocone criterion makes $a$ colimiting. These identities hold on mapping spaces by coherent functoriality of evaluation and composition, not merely on homotopy classes.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.3.6, final-object colimit clause; agent mapping-space argument fixing the specific cocone.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-adjoint-reindexing] to the ordinary adjunction $r^{\mathrm{op}}\dashv j^{\mathrm{op}}$ of Step 1 and the coherent cocone $a$ of Step 3. The ordinary categories are small: their objects are indexed by integers $m\geq-1$ and every morphism set is a set of maps between finite sets. The restricted cocone is therefore colimiting. Its boundary diagram is $\widetilde X\circ N(j^{\mathrm{op}})=X|_{N(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}}}$. Its augmentation is exactly the specified augmentation of $X$: each component is the image of the unique arrow $[n]\to[-1]$ in $\Delta_+^{\mathrm{op}}$, which is also the unique arrow to $t$ used to define $a$. The equality includes every coherence simplex, since both cocones are restrictions of the same nerve of the natural transformation to $t$. Hence $X$ is a colimit diagram with its stated vertex and augmentation.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Propositions 4.1.1.7-8, applied to the explicit ordinary adjunction; compare Lemma 6.1.3.16.

proof.text: Apply the colimit mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] to the small coherent diagram $N(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E$ and the augmentation just proved colimiting. It gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(X_{-1},e)\simeq\lim_{[n]\in\Delta}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(X_n,e)$. The direction of the limit index is $\Delta$, the opposite of the simplicial index $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. The comparison is composition with the augmentation and is natural in $e$, as asserted by the cited node. The same node supplies the small limits in spaces; no colimit-completeness of $\mathcal E$ has been used.

source.place: Mapping-space colimit criterion; HTT 5.1.3.1-2 and 4.2.4.8 in the cited foundation.

proof.text: For a coherent functor $Q:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, put $p_Q=Q\widetilde X:J\to\mathcal F$ and $a_Q=Qa:p_Q\to\Delta_J QX_{-1}$. The cocone $a_Q$ is obtained by applying $p_Q$ to the nerve of the unique-arrow transformation $\mathrm{id}_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}\to\mathrm{const}_t$; its component at $t$ is the identity of $QX_{-1}$. The vertex $t$ is final in $J$, so [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit] supplies a colimiting cocone $b_Q$ for $p_Q$ with vertex $QX_{-1}$ and identity component at $t$. For $f\in\mathcal F$, set $H_Q(f)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal F)}(p_Q,\Delta_J f)$ and let $v_Q:H_Q(f)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F}(QX_{-1},f)$ be evaluation at $t$. By the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], composition with $b_Q$ is an equivalence $c_{b_Q}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F}(QX_{-1},f)\to H_Q(f)$. Since $v_Qc_{b_Q}\simeq1$, $v_Q$ is an equivalence. Composition with $a_Q$ satisfies $v_Qc_{a_Q}\simeq1$ as well, so two-out-of-three makes $c_{a_Q}$ an equivalence. The cocone criterion makes $a_Q$ colimiting. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-adjoint-reindexing] to $r^{\mathrm{op}}\dashv j^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $a_Q$ to obtain a colimiting restricted cocone with vertex $QX_{-1}$. Postcomposition with the simplicial map $Q$ commutes with restriction on every simplex; hence this restricted diagram and cocone are exactly $QX$ and its given augmentation, including all coherences. Only the displayed cocones have been constructed; no existence of other colimits in either target is assumed.

source.place: Remark 4.7.2.4; preservation follows by postcomposing the splitting extension.

Step 1: j adds a least element, r forgets which element is distinguished, j ⊣ r, so r^op ⊣ j^op; checked at m=-1 and n=m=0, and j is not full. Step 2: in the nerve of D^op the vertex t=[-1] is final and the right-pinched mapping spaces are discrete; the cocone a with a_t=1 is the nerve of the unique-arrow transformation. Step 3: final-index plus the cone-calculus criterion, then two-out-of-three, fixes the specific cocone. Step 4: R=j^op, L=r^op is the right direction; the restricted transformation is the nerve of Δ^op×[1]→Δ_+^op→D^op, which strictly equals the augmentation cocone. Step 5: the dual Yoneda clause gives a limit over Δ; universes are enlargeable. Step 6: the argument is written out for QX̃, with no 'similarly' gap. The new node is true by HTT 4.1.3.1 (j/R has initial object (Lj,η_j)) with 4.1.1.7-8, and HTT itself uses this left-adjoint argument. It was tested on the identity adjunction, a terminal object picked out by R, and the empty case. It is statement-only and self-contained, its blueprint from/via is correct, and it has 3 kinds of logged searches with Mathlib's final_of_isRightAdjoint correctly judged ordinary-only. It is not a clause of the item. It is not a duplicate of filtered-cofinal-pullback, anodyne-cocones (needs right anodyne), kan-mapping-restriction (needs full), sifted-nerve or cocone-restriction-initial. Accepted tool_use: lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus as the generic cocone criterion, already a tool use of the same-unit yoneda node.
